name: Clear-bass workflow: low-cut every other part at 100-150 Hz, keep bass notes at 40-80 Hz, then audition three bass-line roles (matching-rhythm, eighth-note pulsing pluck with saw plus same-octave sine and a duck, sustained root per bar) and pick the one that fits
goal: Give a track a clear, satisfying low end by first making room for the bass and then writing the bass line three ways from the chord roots: a matching bass that copies the melody's rhythm, a pulsing eighth-note pluck bass, and a sustained one-note-per-bar bass. Audition all three against the track and keep the one that fits best. The delta against our bass sound-design skills is the bass-line writing roles and the cleanup order, not the patch.

source.title: I Fix A Beginner Producer's Weak Bass (in under 15 minutes)

prerequisites: Any DAW with a piano roll and a spectrum analyzer
Any synth with a saw/sine oscillator, low-pass filter and a spare envelope
A sidechain/volume-duck tool or LFO on gain

inputs.name: track
inputs.description: Song or loop with chords and a melody, before the bass is written

outputs.name: bass_options
outputs.description: Three bass tracks (matching, pulsing, sustained) for A/B choice

outputs.name: clean_mix
outputs.description: Other parts low-cut so the sub range belongs to the bass

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Do not layer several basses while learning; one clear bass is easier to mix.
Keep other instruments out of the sub range: low-cut them somewhere around 100-150 Hz.
Glide on the sustained bass is optional; if used, keep it short and only between notes, never as a random or LFO pitch wobble.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): no random pitch or detune wobble; keep unison detune small and static.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only pad before that.

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: OscillatorNode + GainNode per layer, BiquadFilterNode (lowpass/highpass/allpass) for filters, DelayNode/ConvolverNode for space, AudioParam automation or slow custom LFOs for movement.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Clean up first: mute or delete the old bass layers, thin out muddy duplicate chord layers, reduce heavy reverb on the lead/piano, and leave small gaps between melody notes so it reads more rhythmic.
steps.expect: A clear melody on its own, with space for a bass

steps.action: Low-cut every non-bass instrument at a sweet spot between about 100 and 150 Hz. Check the analyzer: nothing else should spill into the sub range.
steps.expect: Sub range is empty except for the bass

steps.action: Make the bass patch: init synth, shift the octave until the fundamental sits below 100 Hz with notes landing between about 40 and 80 Hz, then use a tight low-pass to focus any waveform toward its lowest frequencies. Try several waveforms; add mid presence by opening the cutoff slightly or with light distortion.
steps.expect: A full, focused bass tone in the 40-80 Hz zone

steps.action: Option 1, matching bass: copy the chord roots to a new track and cut them to the exact rhythm of the melody, so bass and melody hit together.
steps.expect: Bass mirrors the melody rhythm and harmonizes it

steps.action: If any bass note gets lost in the chords or piano, move that note down an octave so the two parts sit in separate ranges.
steps.expect: Every bass note stays audible and clear

steps.action: Option 2, pulsing bass: eighth notes (8 per bar) following the chord roots. Make it a pluck: put a spare envelope on a fully closed cutoff with sustain at zero; use a saw and add a sine at the same octave to thicken it; add a light sidechain-style duck to enhance the pulse.
steps.expect: Tight, driving pluck pulse on the roots (a 16th-note version moves twice as fast)

steps.action: Option 3, sustained bass: one bass note per bar on the chord root. If it holds the energy back, try mono with a short glide between notes, or a wider high-unison saw version, optionally with a filter envelope; remember a mono sub sounds more anchored.
steps.expect: Relaxed, reliable foundation that works with almost any chords

steps.action: Play the track with each option and pick the one that fits: matching moves the melody along, pulsing gives a tighter foundation, sustained is the calmest.
steps.expect: One chosen bass role, the others kept as alternates

verification: No other track has significant energy below about 100 Hz on the analyzer.
The bass fundamentals sit roughly between 40 and 80 Hz.
Three bass versions exist (matching, pulsing eighths, sustained per bar) and all follow the chord roots.
No bass note is masked by the chords; masked notes were moved down an octave.
